summary: TLS session-ticket reuse during proxy rebind leads to partial final SSE fragment + duplicate system/prelude on reconnect
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports streaming SSE responses from /v1/chat sometimes terminate with only a prefix (no closing metadata/event) and their client reconnect ends up receiving a duplicate 'system' prelude and a partial final paragraph. Impact: End users see truncated guidance text and repeated assistant/system messages; customer is on Dedicated in us-east and uses an edge proxy in front of the Redwood endpoint. Environment: Arcadia Health, Dedicated reservation, VPC peered egress through customer's Fastly edge. Steps to reproduce: 1) Launch a long streaming chat session against redwood-v1-large in prod:us-east behind customer's Fastly config. 2) Trigger a high-token response (>800 tokens) and then force a short network path change on the client (simulate 0rtt/TLS rebind or NAT port change). 3) Observe SSE stream: stream closes with no end-event, client reconnects, and the first few events contain system/prelude and duplicated metadata followed by a truncated final paragraph. Logs and evidence: - Customer trace ID: arc-20260305-7a9b - Edge capture (Fastly): session ticket reuse + connection rebind at 2026-03-05T14:12:03Z showing upstream RST followed by new TLS handshake. - Server logs (serving-runtime): connection closed with unfinished chunk write; last write returned EPIPE in worker-17. - Console tracing: request routed to g-serve-10, prefetched KV-cache primed for conversation, no explicit model error. - Repro run attached in customer upload (link in comment). Immediate customer impact: High — production users intermittently get truncated responses and duplicated system messages causing confusion in clinical guidance flows.

Business context: Arcadia Health uses streaming to deliver multi-paragraph clinical summaries; truncated final sentences are safety-affecting and need reliable mitigation.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a long SSE chat session to /v1/chat with model redwood-v1-large behind customer's Fastly edge
Force a short transport interruption (NAT rebind or TLS ticket reuse) while stream is mid-response
Observe that stream does not emit end-event and client reconnect receives duplicated system/prelude packets and the dialogue ends mid-sentence
observed_behavior: Missing end-of-stream event in SSE after connection rebind
Client receives repeated system prelude on reconnect
Final paragraph truncated mid-sentence and not re-sent
expected_behavior: SSE stream should always emit an end marker before socket close or server should provide resume delta
Reconnect should not replay initial system envelope for the same session
Final content should either be completed or resumed cleanly
logs: server: worker-17: write error EPIPE at 2026-03-05T14:12:03Z
edge(fastly): observed TLS ticket resumption and connection handoff at 2026-03-05T14:12:03Z
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-05: Opened with customer-supplied capture. Customer believes issue started after they rolled a new Fastly VCL that enabled aggressive session-ticket reuse.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-05: Assigned for deeper investigation. Initial hypothesis: edge rebind + upstream half-close causing worker to abort write before emission of final end-event. Will reproduce in lab with Fastly-like rebind simulator.

Arcadia Health (Customer) 2026-03-06: Provided tcpdump and Fastly edge logs (uploaded to secure bucket). Not seeing any application-level errors on their side; behavior started after VCL change two days ago.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-07: Reproduced in staging with simulated session-ticket reuse: observed server write returning EPIPE when client initiates 0-RTT session rebind during long-tail token emission. Also saw initial event batch re-sent by edge during reconnect path which the client interprets as duplicate system message.

Dev (runtime) 2026-03-08: Proposed patch to guard against replaying initial system envelope when a resume-reconnect contains a resumable conversation token. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8142
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-09: Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer; waiting for engineering patch rollout to staging for verification.
investigation_notes: Repro notes: staging harness with 'fastly-sim' replays scenario at ~70% when simulating TLS ticket reuse and forced NAT rebind

Root cause hypothesis: combination of edge-level partial replay + server worker write failure leads to stream finishing without emitting SSE end-event; reconnect path causes edge to inject a prelude packet (system envelope) from cache or replay buffer

Worker behavior: when write fails mid-chunk we currently close connection without enqueuing an explicit end-event; client SDK treats reconnect as a new session and consumes prelude events that were re-sent by edge
Client behavior: Arcadia client library re-applies session prelude when it sees server-origin 'system' event; it does not de-duplicate on message-id
temporary_workarounds: Customer: increase Fastly VCL to not replay upstream responses on handshake rebind (disable response caching for /v1/chat streams)
Customer: configure client to treat 'system' envelopes idempotently for a short dedup window (example: ignore repeated system messages with identical content within 5s)
Support: instruct client to enable keepalive pings so the edge path is less likely to rebind mid-stream
resolution_notes: 2026-03-08 engineering patch created (PR #8142) to: 1) ensure serving-runtime emits a final end-event before hard-closing sockets on write failures where possible; 2) add server-side guard preventing replay of the initial system envelope on resume flows if session state indicates message was already delivered
2026-03-09: Patch merged to staging. SRE to run canary with Arcadia test harness and Fastly-sim. If staging pass, rollout to prod for dedicated customers by 2026-03-12
Customer mitigation advised and acknowledged. Arcadia will coordinate a temporary VCL rollback if staging fails
final_resolution: Pending rollout to production. Engineering has merged a staging patch that addresses two behaviours: emitting explicit SSE end-event on write failure and gating replayed system messages during resume. SRE will validate with Arcadia's test harness behind their Fastly configuration before scheduling a prod push. No permanent data loss expected; workaround reduces incidence until prod patch is live.
postmortem_actions: Add a guard in serving-runtime to enqueue an end-event whenever possible on write error
Add dedup metadata to system envelopes (message-id) so clients/edges can dedupe on reconnect
Document recommended Fastly VCL snippet in Confluence runbook to avoid response replay for streaming endpoints
